key_insight: Phase-adapted shallow neural dictionaries achieve N^(-1/2) Sobolev approximation bounds, while matching a chirped target’s phase reduces the phase-dependent growth of the stated upper bound.
engineering_relevance: Encoding known oscillatory phase into neural features offers a principled approach to approximating chirped signals without changing the guaranteed N^(-1/2) rate.
method: Define weighted STSAFT-modulation spaces and connect them to classical modulation spaces through chirp factorization.
Construct a transform-adapted neural dictionary and prove bounded-domain and global N-term approximation estimates.
Analyze phase matching for fixed-scale chirp families to sharpen the phase-dependent upper bound.
evidence_signal: Four numerical experiments examine model comparison, dictionary-size error decay, phase mismatch, and the obstruction caused by restricted translations.
watch_item: Global guarantees require unrestricted translations; phase-mismatch comparisons concern upper bounds, not thresholds for optimal approximation error.
paper_title: Weighted STSAFT-Modulation Spaces and Approximation by Phase-Adapted Neural Networks
